userStories.title: Encrypted provider credential storage
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the encrypted provider vault persistence, configuration, secret-store interface and injectable module.

**Motivation** — Today each runner needs every provider credential stored on the machine (`nax auth`).

**Approach** — Model `ProviderCredential` (`id`, `scope` `GLOBAL|PROJECT|REPO` as a string, `scopeKey`, `projectId?`, `repoId?`, `providerId`, `name`, `encryptedKey`, `last4`, `fingerprint`, `createdById`, `updatedById`, `disabledAt?`, timestamps), `@@unique([scopeKey, providerId])`, `@@index([projectId])`, `@@index([repoId])`. Model `ProviderCredentialIssue` (`id`, `jobId`, `credentialId`, `fingerprint`, `createdAt`), `@@unique([jobId, credentialId, fingerprint])`. `providerId` matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,47}$`; `name` 1-64 chars. A `SecretStore` interface (`seal(plaintext) -> { encryptedKey, last4, fingerprint }`, `open(encryptedKey) -> plaintext`) with one implementation, `LocalSecretStore`, over `encryptToken`/`decryptToken` and the config namespace `providerCredentials` (`PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`).

Uniqueness uses a computed `scopeKey` string (`global`, `project:<projectId>`, `repo:<repoId>`) with `@@unique([scopeKey, providerId])`, because Postgres treats NULL columns as distinct. Fingerprint = first 12 hex chars of HMAC-SHA256(master key, plaintext key); `last4` = last 4 chars of the key. Relations: `ProviderCredential.projectId` and `repoId` reference `Project` and `FleetRepo` with `onDelete: Cascade`; `createdById`/`updatedById` are plain strings (no FK), as on other fleet rows. New env `PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (64 hex chars), separate from `VCS_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. Unset = the vault is off: management writes refuse with 503 and hand-outs answer `vault_off`; the API still boots.

Implement the repository behind PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REPOSITORY with transaction-aware PrismaService and generated Prisma imports; add schema inverse relations and a committed additive migration. Register the config namespace in application config loading. The module must compile without a master key and exports no repository token; subsequent service work belongs to US-002.

**Scope** — In: models, migration, config namespace/env validation, SecretStore/LocalSecretStore, repository contract/implementation and ProviderCredentialsModule wiring. Out: service resolution/CRUD (US-002), management controllers/permissions (US-003–005), sync issuance (US-006). HashiCorp Vault, OpenBao and cloud KMS backends are not built; only the local encrypted `SecretStore` exists. Re-encrypting stored keys under a new master key (master key rotation) is not built.

**Interface** — `encryptToken(plaintext: string, masterKey: string): string`; `decryptToken(ciphertext: string, masterKey: string): string`; `SecretStore` — `seal(plaintext) -> { encryptedKey, last4, fingerprint }`, `open(encryptedKey) -> plaintext`; repository injection token `PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REPOSITORY`. Use the existing AES-256-GCM iv:tag:ciphertext implementation rather than replacing it.

userStories.title: Resolve and issue the most specific key
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Implement the vault service for active scoped resolution, safe decryption and shared create/update/remove domain operations.

**Motivation** — Setting up a runner, rotating a key, or keeping separate billing per project means touching every machine, and nothing records which job used which key.

**Approach** — `ProviderCredentialsService.resolve({ projectId, repoId | null, providerId })` returns the active (`disabledAt` null) REPO key for `repoId`, else the PROJECT key, else the GLOBAL key, else null.

`ProviderCredentialsService` with `isEnabled`, `resolve` (REPO, then PROJECT, then GLOBAL, active rows only), `issueKey` (decrypt for a hand-out) and `create`/`update`/`remove` domain methods used by the routes (key validation, sealing, `P2002` -> duplicate). A key is 16-8192 characters with no whitespace (16 keeps `last4` to at most a quarter of the key). `providerId` matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,47}$`; `name` 1-64 chars.

Vault off means resolve returns null without querying storage and all domain writes refuse with 503 fleet.providerCredentials.vaultOff. A unique-constraint violation (Prisma `P2002`) maps to 409 `fleet.providerCredentials.duplicate`. Ciphertext cannot be decrypted: Hand-out answers `none` and logs a warning with the credential id only. Implement issueKey as nullable plaintext so sync can map a decryption failure to none; never log ciphertext, plaintext, or the crypto exception message. PATCH domain behavior supports independent name, key rotation and disabled boolean changes; name-only retains fingerprint. Extend ProviderCredentialsModule to provide/export the service, keeping its repository private.

**Scope** — In: validation/sealing, active scope lookup, decryption boundary, vault-off guard, safe duplicate mapping and write primitives. Out: HTTP/approval/audit/activity adapters (US-003–005), issue attribution/runner transport (US-006). Spend caps or rate limits per provider key are not enforced; existing C1 job budgets are unchanged. An LLM proxy or gateway in front of providers (one koda key for all providers) is not built.

**Interface** — `ProviderCredentialsService.resolve({ projectId, repoId | null, providerId })`; `isEnabled()`; `issueKey(credential)`; `create`/`update`/`remove`. `issueKey` returns plaintext or null; `resolve` returns the chosen credential or null. LocalSecretStore and PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REPOSITORY are supplied by US-001.

userStories.title: Create and list GLOBAL provider keys
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose permission-checked GLOBAL key creation and write-only metadata listing through approval-aware API routes.

**Motivation** — Today each runner needs every provider credential stored on the machine (`nax auth`).

**Approach** — Global routes `GET|POST /fleet/provider-credentials`, `PATCH|DELETE /fleet/provider-credentials/:id` (`fleet.credential.read|create|update|delete`). Every response row is `{ id, scope, projectId, repoId, providerId, name, last4, fingerprint, disabled, createdBy, updatedAt }`, never the key. Writes run through route commands (approval-gated, `redeem.redact` with `redactSecret`), record `FleetActivity` (`credential.created|rotated|updated|disabled|enabled|deleted`, entityType `provider_credential`, entityId the credential id) and an audit entry (`AuditRecorder.record` with the route key). A unique-constraint violation (Prisma `P2002`) maps to 409 `fleet.providerCredentials.duplicate`.

This story implements GET and POST only; US-004 adds PATCH/DELETE. Add catalog keys fleet.credential.create|update|delete in NEW_KEY_SCOPES (global), retaining existing fleet.credential.read. Owner/Admin manage GLOBAL keys. The prefix fleet.credential. is already high risk. Update catalog mirrors/count and role matrix so only Owner/Admin inherit global writes. `FleetEntityType` adds `'provider_credential'` without changing other members; update the schema comment.

Writes follow the `vcs.connection.create` precedent exactly: route commands whose `redeem.redact` replaces the key with `redactSecret(key)`, so no approval request row carries the key. Use @ApprovalGated({ redeem: true }), @ApprovalRedeemHeader() and routeGate.run with projectId null. Redemption seals the key resubmitted in the redeem body. Activity/audit share the mutation transaction. `FleetActivityService.record(entry)` rejects payload keys matching `/token|secret|key|password|credential/i`, so payloads use `providerId`, `scope`, `name`, `fingerprint` only. Add en/zh API providerCredentials translations and route/module registration. Regenerate OpenAPI and generated CLI via bun run generate, never by hand; extend existing endpoint e2e create/list happy and error cases.

**Scope** — In: GLOBAL GET/POST, DTOs, new write permissions, create route command/redaction, created activity/audit and translations. Out: PATCH/DELETE execution (US-004), project routes (US-005), sync hand-outs (US-006), provider-key CLI or MCP tools.

**Interface** — `GET|POST /fleet/provider-credentials`; POST body `{ providerId, name, key }`; response `{ id, scope, projectId, repoId, providerId, name, last4, fingerprint, disabled, createdBy, updatedAt }`; `routeCommand({ key, variant, parse, redeem: { redact }, run })`; `AuditRecorder.record({ key, resourceType, resourceId, projectId?, summary })`.

userStories.title: Rotate, disable and delete GLOBAL provider keys
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add approved GLOBAL key rotation, metadata edits, disable/enable and deletion without returning saved secrets.

**Motivation** — Setting up a runner, rotating a key, or keeping separate billing per project means touching every machine, and nothing records which job used which key.

**Approach** — PATCH takes any of `name`, `key` (rotate), `disabled` (boolean). Every response row is `{ id, scope, projectId, repoId, providerId, name, last4, fingerprint, disabled, createdBy, updatedAt }`, never the key. Writes run through route commands (approval-gated, `redeem.redact` with `redactSecret`), record `FleetActivity` (`credential.created|rotated|updated|disabled|enabled|deleted`, entityType `provider_credential`, entityId the credential id) and an audit entry (`AuditRecorder.record` with the route key).

PATCH and DELETE on `/fleet/provider-credentials/:id`; route commands for update (key redacted) and delete; activity and audit. Credential id of another scope on a project or global route: 404. Scope/provider identity is not reassigned through PATCH. Rotation changes fingerprint/last4/encryptedKey; name-only keeps fingerprint; disabled changes disabledAt and response disabled. Emit credential.rotated, credential.updated, credential.disabled, credential.enabled and credential.deleted as applicable, with exactly providerId, scope, name, fingerprint payload fields and no secret-bearing audit text. Use the US-002 service primitives, keep all writes guarded by vault enabled, and keep the mutation/activity/audit atomic. Update command redaction only when a new key was supplied; approval storage never holds the plaintext. Regenerate OpenAPI/CLI via bun run generate and extend existing endpoint e2e rotate/disable/delete happy and error cases.

Revocation latency: after a key is disabled or deleted, a running nax keeps its current lease until `expiresAt` (nax-agent serves the last good lease when the helper fails), so a running job is cut off at most 10 minutes later. Do not introduce immediate process interruption here.

**Scope** — In: GLOBAL PATCH/DELETE, update/delete route commands, metadata projections and transactional activity/audit. Out: project/repo lifecycle (US-005), sync denial/renewal (US-006/008), runner helper revocation behavior (US-009).

**Interface** — `PATCH|DELETE /fleet/provider-credentials/:id`; PATCH `{ name?, key?, disabled? }`; route keys `fleet.credential.update` and `fleet.credential.delete`; management response projection remains unchanged from US-003.

userStories.title: Manage PROJECT and REPO provider keys
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let project admins manage PROJECT defaults and per-REPO overrides through tenant-isolated approval-aware routes.

**Motivation** — Setting up a runner, rotating a key, or keeping separate billing per project means touching every machine, and nothing records which job used which key.

**Approach** — Project routes `GET|POST /projects/:slug/provider-credentials`, `PATCH|DELETE /projects/:slug/provider-credentials/:id` (`project.credential.read|create|update|delete`); a POST with `repoId` creates a REPO key for a repo of that project; the project routes see only that project's PROJECT and REPO rows (any other id is 404). PATCH takes any of `name`, `key` (rotate), `disabled` (boolean). Every response row is `{ id, scope, projectId, repoId, providerId, name, last4, fingerprint, disabled, createdBy, updatedAt }`, never the key. Writes run through route commands (approval-gated, `redeem.redact` with `redactSecret`), record `FleetActivity` (`credential.created|rotated|updated|disabled|enabled|deleted`, entityType `provider_credential`, entityId the credential id) and an audit entry (`AuditRecorder.record` with the route key). A unique-constraint violation (Prisma `P2002`) maps to 409 `fleet.providerCredentials.duplicate`.

Permission keys: `fleet.credential.create|update|delete` (global; the prefix is already high risk) and `project.credential.read|create|update|delete` (project; `project.credential.` joins `HIGH_RISK_PREFIXES`). Scope writes here use only project keys; US-003 owns global keys. Add the project catalog keys/mirrors and role snapshot: Project Admin all four, other project roles read through *.read and no write. read risk is low; writes high. ProjectMembershipGuard and RequiresGuard remain the authorization boundary. REPO key for a repo of another project: 404 `fleet.repos`. Credential id of another scope on a project or global route: 404. Do not leak whether another project's credential exists.

Extend shared commands with pinned project scope, @ApprovalGated({ redeem: true }) and redemption header; redact incoming key for agent approvals, use resubmitted key on redemption. Record projectId on activity/audit, using the same non-secret payload as GLOBAL writes. Regenerate OpenAPI and CLI client via bun run generate and extend existing endpoint e2e coverage for PROJECT/REPO lifecycle with happy/error per route.

**Scope** — In: project GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE, PROJECT/REPO creation, membership checks, catalog/role integration, scoped commands and activity/audit. Out: GLOBAL management (US-003/004), scope-precedence transport (US-006), project settings UI (US-013).

**Interface** — `GET|POST /projects/:slug/provider-credentials`; `PATCH|DELETE /projects/:slug/provider-credentials/:id`; POST `{ providerId, name, key, repoId? }`; PATCH `{ name?, key?, disabled? }`; response is the shared secret-free ProviderCredentialDto.

userStories.title: Hand provider keys to runners through sync
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the optional sync protocol to grant scoped provider leases with fencing and deduplicated job attribution.

**Motivation** — Setting up a runner, rotating a key, or keeping separate billing per project means touching every machine, and nothing records which job used which key.

**Approach** — `SyncService` handles `providerRequests` like `tokenRequests`: fence (a stale epoch abandons, as for tokens), job state in `RUNNER_HELD_STATES` (else `job_not_active`), vault off (`vault_off`), scope (thread job: `findThreadCredentialScope`; fleet job: the job's `projectId`/`repoId`), resolve (null or undecryptable = `none`), else a grant with `account = koda:<scope lowercase>:<name>` and `expiresAt = now + 10 min`. In the same transaction it inserts `ProviderCredentialIssue` with skip-on-duplicate and, when a row was inserted, records `credential.issued` (actor `RUNNER`/runnerId, entityType `provider_credential`, entityId the credential id, `jobId`, `projectId`, payload `{ providerId, scope, name, fingerprint }`). A response with any provider grant or error skips the long-poll wait.

Hand-out lease `expiresAt = now + 10 min`. Attribution dedupe uses a `ProviderCredentialIssue` row unique on (job, credential, fingerprint); a new row records one `credential.issued` activity. Thread jobs resolve from the thread's own `projectId` and `repoId` (`repoId` null for PROJECT and WORKSPACE threads; a WORKSPACE thread's anchor `projectId` is non-null, so its PROJECT key applies); fleet jobs from `FleetJob.projectId` and `FleetJob.repoId`. Leave findThreadTokenScope unchanged. Here abandonment means FenceService queues ABANDON for the requesting runner/job/epoch with reason stale_lease; it is not a transition of FleetJob.state.

Add wire types to packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts and API type-only protocol bridge; make all new envelope fields optional for old peers. Parse a maximum 64 provider requests, validating jobId, epoch and provider regex. Lock each job before FenceService.holds and abandonment; never disclose a key before ownership/state checks. Issue row and activity commit together with duplicate-safe insertion, no forge HTTP or long-poll inside that transaction. Add the provider module to SyncModule and service stubs to existing token-fence/token-purpose tests, preserving their assertions. This story depends only on US-002: coordinate the additive provider_credential type with US-003 without changing the binding DAG or importing management routes into the sync boundary.

**Scope** — In: wire types, parser, new thread credential scope query/interface, fenced sync grants/errors and issuance attribution. Out: management routes (US-003–005), runner cache/socket (US-008), helper implementation (US-009), key usage billing.

**Interface** — `SyncRequest.providerRequests?: ProviderKeyRequest[]` with `ProviderKeyRequest { jobId: string; leaseEpoch: number; providerId: string }`; `SyncResponse.providerKeys?: ProviderKeyGrant[]` with `ProviderKeyGrant { jobId; providerId; key; expiresAt: string (ISO); account: string; fingerprint: string }`; `SyncResponse.providerKeyErrors?: ProviderKeyError[]` with `ProviderKeyError { jobId; providerId; reason: 'none' | 'job_not_active' | 'vault_off' }`. New repository sibling `findThreadCredentialScope(jobId): Promise<{ projectId: string; repoId: string | null } | null>`. `FenceService.holds(job, runnerId, leaseEpoch)` remains authoritative.

[integration] That grant's expiresAt is 10 minutes after the sync time.

userStories.title: Runner provider-key sockets and cache
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add in-memory provider leases, per-job provider-key sockets and real sync-loop transport without changing git credential sockets.

**Motivation** — Today each runner needs every provider credential stored on the machine (`nax auth`).

**Approach** — `CredentialBroker.serveProviderKeys(job)` opens one provider-key socket per job and epoch. Its reply for `provider <id>` queues a `ProviderKeyRequest` in a `ProviderKeyCache` (in memory, mirroring `TokenCache`), wakes the sync loop, waits up to 55 s for the grant, serves a cached grant until 60 s before `expiresAt` (ISO converted to epoch ms), and remembers which providers it served the job: once served, a later `none` becomes `revoked`. `releaseProviderKeys(job)` closes it and forgets the job.

Each job gets its own provider-key socket, separate from the git credential socket, open for the whole job (git credentials are released after checkout; provider keys are needed for every model call). `BrokerDeps` gains an optional provider-key cache; provider-key sockets live in their own map, never in `servers` (so `release`'s sibling check for `<jobDir>/bin` ignores them). `serveProviderKeys(job: JobRow): Promise<string>` opens, once per job and epoch, at `socketPathFor(dir, runnerId, jobId, leaseEpoch, 'provider-keys')` and returns its path, whatever the clone URL. `providerKeyGranted(job, providerId): Promise<boolean>` uses the same lookup the socket uses, true on a grant. `releaseProviderKeys(job)` closes the socket, drops the job's cached grants and served set. `closeAll` also closes provider-key sockets.

Keep CredentialServer.listen/get behavior unchanged; add listenProviderKeys using private socket permissions and existing atomic socket replacement/inode-safe close. A socket accepts only `provider <providerId>\n`, with `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,47}$`. Pending expiry is error, never an invented grant. Initial none (including an initially disabled vault) can decline via the helper; after a grant, none becomes revoked so no identity switch occurs. State and waiters are keyed by job/epoch/provider and never journaled/logged/persisted. Bind grants to the originating request epoch because responses do not carry leaseEpoch. Keep other epochs untouched on release.

SyncLoop gains optional providerRequests/onProviderKeys deps and is non-idle while provider requests are queued; newly queued requests wake it as token needs do. Wire cache apply using the originating sync request snapshot, the broker and onNeed listener in daemon.ts, including listener teardown. Integrate with sync/batch.ts request budgeting and the 64-request bound rather than bypassing the 1 MiB envelope budget. Keep existing daemon-thread wiring assertions unchanged when extending fakes. Put 55 s and 60 s timing constants in daemon/tuning.ts with test clock overrides.

**Scope** — In: provider server protocol, cache, optional broker methods, sync/batch/daemon transport and shutdown. Out: nax exec helper and executor env (US-009), config commands/probe (US-010), thread session source (US-011). Secrecy from the agent is not claimed: the agent's Bash runs as the runner uid and can reach the job's provider-key socket. Value redaction of runner-shipped job logs, thread logs, bundles and diagnostics for served provider keys is not done; the key is never in the job env or on disk, and nax-agent's own redaction is unchanged.

**Interface** — `CredentialServer.listenProviderKeys(path, providerReply: (providerId: string) => Promise<ProviderReply>)`; `ProviderReply = { ok: true; key: string; expiresAt: number; account: string } | { ok: false; reason: 'none' | 'revoked' | 'error' | 'bad request' }`. `CredentialProvider` gains OPTIONAL `serveProviderKeys?`, `providerKeyGranted?` and `releaseProviderKeys?`; callers skip them when absent. `SyncLoop` optional deps: `providerRequests?(): readonly ProviderKeyRequest[]` and `onProviderKeys?(grants, errors)`; provider cache application must retain the matching originating request epochs internally.

userStories.title: nax exec helper and fleet job environment
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Implement nax's provider-cred exec contract and connect provider sockets to all fleet executor paths and readoption.

**Motivation** — The nax side is ready: nax-agent 0.91.7 (koda's pin) ships the exec helper contract and a per-session credential source.

**Approach** — The host executor calls `serveProviderKeys(job)` and puts `KODA_PROVIDER_CRED_SOCKET=<path>` in the nax env at both spawn sites (`spawn`, which covers RUN, PLAN and REVIEW, and `spawnFixStep`), re-serves it in `resumeCredentials` (a readopted nax keeps its deterministic socket path), and calls `releaseProviderKeys(job)` in both `cleanup()` and `releaseCredentials()`. The config job serves before it builds `naxEnv` and releases in its own cleanup. The helper `koda-runner provider-cred [--socket <path>] get` reads the nax request from stdin; the socket is `--socket` when given, else `KODA_PROVIDER_CRED_SOCKET`; it maps: neither given -> decline; `none` -> decline; ok -> the api-key reply; `revoked`, `error`, `bad request`, socket failure -> exit 1 with one stderr line and nothing on stdout.

The helper contract: argv `[...command, "get"]`; stdin `{"version":1,"providerId":"<id>"}`; reply `{"version":1,"kind":"api-key","key":"...","expiresAt":<epoch ms>,"account":"..."}` or `{"version":1,"decline":true}`; non-zero exit = failure. A failure while a lease is held serves the last good lease until its `expiresAt`. A decline for a provider that already holds a lease is invalid. `key` <= 8192 chars; `account` <= 200 chars. Helper timeout 60000 ms (nax's schema maximum); the socket holds a provider reply open up to 55 s.

Dispatch provider-cred before Commander alongside git-cred/shim; isolate stdin/stdout/socket/env/stderr through injectable dependencies for tests. Only the socket path, never the key, enters the nax environment or argv. Override inherited socket env with the current job's returned path. Optional provider methods mean existing acquire/release-only fakes keep today's env. Invoke release independently of git release failures, including config job failure cleanup; preserve nax forge-token-file behavior unrelated to this provider vault. A first request with vault_off ultimately declines through the broker's initial none mapping. Revocation latency: after a key is disabled or deleted, a running nax keeps its current lease until `expiresAt` (nax-agent serves the last good lease when the helper fails), so a running job is cut off at most 10 minutes later.

**Scope** — In: helper implementation/dispatch, socket client, both host spawn envs, resume/cleanup/release and config-job lifecycle. Out: writing nax global config (US-010), native sessions (US-011). Value redaction of runner-shipped job logs, thread logs, bundles and diagnostics for served provider keys is not done; the key is never in the job env or on disk, and nax-agent's own redaction is unchanged. Revocation does not interrupt a running nax before its current lease expires (at most 10 minutes).

**Interface** — `runProviderCred(['get'])`; `runProviderCred(['--socket', <path>, 'get'])`; CLI `koda-runner provider-cred [--socket <path>] get`; socket request `provider <providerId>\n`; nax exec reply and decline schema above. `dispatchInternal(argv)` additionally recognizes `provider-cred`.

**Goal** — Add explicit atomic nax helper configuration commands and report whether the installed global helper is koda's.

**Motivation** — Today each runner needs every provider credential stored on the machine (`nax auth`).

**Approach** — `koda-runner vault enable` writes `auth: { source: "exec", exec: { command: [...self, "provider-cred"], timeoutMs: 60000 }, onChange: "warn" }` into `<naxHome>/config.json`, keeping every other key, via a temp file + rename; `vault disable` removes `auth`. The runner never edits nax config on its own; `koda-runner vault enable|disable` does, atomically. nax `auth` is global-only: read only from `<NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR>/config.json`, shape `auth: { source: "file" | "exec", exec?: { command: string[], timeoutMs: number }, onChange: "warn" | "refuse" }`. userStories.title: Native thread sessions use koda keys
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve the native session's provider before open and supply per-session exec credentials while preserving machine-local fallback and ACP isolation.

**Motivation** — The nax side is ready: nax-agent 0.91.7 (koda's pin) ships the exec helper contract and a per-session credential source.

**Approach** — `ThreadJobRun` calls `serveProviderKeys(row)` before both `sessions.open` call sites (the REPO path and `runProject`, so REPO, PROJECT and WORKSPACE threads alike), passes `providerKeys: { socket, granted: (p) => broker.providerKeyGranted(row, p) }` into every `open`, and calls `releaseProviderKeys(row)` in `start()`'s `finally` and in `abandon()`. The factory derives `providerId` from the session model id (text before the first `/`; the runner default model when the thread pins none; a model id with no `/` gets no koda key) and, when `granted` is true, sets the per-session exec `credentials`; otherwise it opens without `credentials` (process-wide store, machine-local). ACP threads never consult it.

`OpenThreadSessionOptions` adds `providerKeys?: { socket: string; granted(providerId: string): Promise<boolean> }`; native options carry `credentials: { kind: 'exec', command: [...self, 'provider-cred', '--socket', socket], timeoutMs: 60000 }` when `granted` resolves true for the session model's provider. nax-agent per-session source: `NativeBackendOptions.credentials?: CredentialSource`, where the exec member is `{ kind: "exec"; command: readonly string[]; timeoutMs?: number; onChange?: "warn" | "refuse" }` (no file fallback).

Use the model selected by existing pinned/default model validation, not the effort-decorated model text. Add optional self argv to the existing ThreadSessionFactoryOptions and pass it from daemon wiring, defaulting through the existing selfCommand() helper for construction sites that omit it. Do not make existing factory constructors supply a new required argument. Keep ACP branch before all provider lookup; no provider key may reach an ACP backend. Existing CredentialProvider fakes with acquire/release continue working because all provider methods are optional, and missing providerKeys preserves current backend options. Ensure failures before or during session open still release sockets in finally, and abandonment remains bounded. Retain current thread profiles, protected paths, session resume/create behavior, turn handling and no-process-reaping invariants.

**Scope** — In: optional session options, native provider lookup/exec source, both thread open call sites, release/finally/abandon and self-command wiring. Out: fleet process env (US-009), global config edits (US-010). ACP thread backends (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) keep their own sign-ins on the runner host and never receive koda keys. A model switch inside one open native session to a provider koda holds no key for is not re-resolved; the next session open re-resolves (the per-session exec source has no file fallback).

**Interface** — `OpenThreadSessionOptions.providerKeys?: { socket: string; granted(providerId: string): Promise<boolean> }`; `ThreadSessionFactory.open`; `NativeBackendOptions.credentials?: CredentialSource`; exec command `[...self argv, 'provider-cred', '--socket', socket]`, timeoutMs 60000. userStories.title: Rulings refuse items nax can never settle
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Refuse CI-item rulings and draft PRs known to lack the nax item index before creating or approving ineffective rulings.

**Motivation** — The ruling looks accepted until a billed FIX reports `skipped: unknown-item`.

**Approach** — `ruleTarget` refuses `kind === 'ci'` (no forge read). `assertItemIndex(target)`, for a GitHub repo with an installation id, mints the thread-read token, calls new `GitHubAppClient.listIssueComments(token, owner, name, number)` (`GET /repos/{o}/{n}/issues/{number}/comments?per_page=100`, 5 s timeout, returns bodies), and refuses `noItemIndex` only when the page has fewer than 100 comments and none contains `<!-- nax-bot:v1 key=w-index -->`.

The `w-index` pre-check runs before the ruling transaction, matches the exact nax marker `<!-- nax-bot:v1 key=w-index -->`, reads one page of 100 comments with a 5 s timeout, and fails open on any forge error or a full page with no marker. No author check: a planted marker only restores today's behaviour (a later skip).

`RulingJobTarget`, `findTarget` and `lockTarget` add `repo: { provider: string; owner: string; name: string; githubInstallationId: bigint | null }`. `FleetPrRulingsService.ruleTarget(projectId, jobId, dto)` also refuses `notRulable` (item kind `ci`). A new `preflight(projectId, jobId, dto)` runs `ruleTarget` then `assertItemIndex(target)` (the forge check); all three callers (the controller, the ruling route command and the assistant `pr-ruling-tools.ts`) call `preflight` before `create`, never inside `create`'s transaction. Both `RulingJobTarget` producers, `findTarget` and `lockTarget`, populate `repo`.

Retain create's lock/re-read ruleTarget checks and existing notDraft/notLatest/unknownItem/invalidText/settled refusal precedence. Do not put forge I/O in that transaction or weaken transactional eligibility rechecks. Assistant preview and execute both need preflight and refusal mapping for the new codes. listIssueComments must use FleetHttpClient with no redirects, an explicit 5 s timeout, the supplied bearer token and provider-error mapping on non-200; mintThreadReadToken already supplies pull_requests:read. FleetHttpClient.request currently accepts only method, url, headers and optional body, so extend that existing method with an optional per-request timeout options parameter for this 5000 ms read. Existing calls without an override must still use config.httpTimeoutMs, preserve non-2xx status returns and refuse redirects. Do not change its default timeout globally or introduce a second forge HTTP implementation. Catch forge mint/read failures for fail-open, but do not swallow the deliberate noItemIndex conflict. Return only first-page comment bodies; do not add pagination or author verification. Update API en/zh fleet.rulings.notRulable/noItemIndex and existing ruling fixtures to non-ci accepted items, preserving existing assertions and snapshot repo shape.

**Scope** — In: target repo projection, ci refusal, external preflight, GitHub comments client and controller/command/assistant wiring. Out: web Rule/skip copy (US-015), provider vault stories (US-001–013), changes to nax settling logic. GitLab merge requests get no `w-index` pre-check; rulings are GitHub-only today. The `w-index` pre-check does not verify the marker comment's author.

**Interface** — `preflight(projectId, jobId, dto)`; `assertItemIndex(target)`; `GitHubAppClient.listIssueComments(token, owner, name, number)`; `repo: { provider: string; owner: string; name: string; githubInstallationId: bigint | null }`; conflicts `fleet.rulings.notRulable` and `fleet.rulings.noItemIndex`.

analysis:
SECOND-PASS ADVERSARIAL AUDIT
Enumerated and retained all 178 explicit spec acceptance criteria in their original stories: US-001=13, US-002=14, US-003=14, US-004=13, US-005=14, US-006=15, US-007=8, US-008=14, US-009=13, US-010=9, US-011=11, US-012=13, US-013=9, US-014=14, US-015=4. Original criteria remain first in each array; failure-table and regression assertions follow them. Qualifiers retained include stale git-token abandonment equivalence, matching grants and epoch-ms conversion, optional credential fakes, the abandon-path parenthesis, readoption's same deterministic socket path, unchanged fingerprint on rename, exact activity payloads, no repository export, no plaintext response, and the exact unknown-item English copy. Every story has an observable negative path; explicit native invalid-model behavior is also pinned. No deprecated grep/file/verbatim AC tags occur in the spec. All 17 feature exclusions are retained verbatim, with no story-local work promoted to feature exclusions. Binding IDs, workdirs and dependencies remain unchanged.
The audit corrected permission-check syntax to the real usePermissions.ts public shape: useGlobalPermissions()/useProjectPermissions(slug) return a Permissions object whose permissions.value has the has method (apps/web/composables/usePermissions.ts:33-42, :75-81), not a direct has method. No new permission composable is needed. The US-008 cached-repeat fixture explicitly sits outside the final 60-second renewal margin, so it cannot contradict the next AC requiring renewal inside that margin. FenceService.abandon queues a runner ABANDON command with reason stale_lease and does not transition FleetJob.state (apps/api/src/fleet/sync/fence.service.ts:22-30); the stale-epoch AC now names that actual observable behavior while keeping its regression qualifier.
FleetHttpClient.request currently has only method/url/headers/body and uses config.httpTimeoutMs for all requests (apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/fleet-http-client.ts:14-20). US-014 must extend that existing method with an OPTIONAL per-request timeout override for the 5000 ms comments read, keeping all current callers, redirect refusal, provider error mapping and default timeout unchanged. Do not pretend a timeout option already exists or switch to raw fetch. ThreadSessionFactoryOptions currently lacks self argv (apps/runner/src/thread/session-factory.ts:28-33); US-011 adds optional injectable self argv with a fallback through the existing self-command mechanism so old construction sites remain valid. Existing config-job cleanup at apps/runner/src/executor/config-job/config-job.ts:54-59 restores the clone but has no provider cleanup yet: add a finally around the new provider lifecycle without changing the returned config-job result.
Regression assertions now make the spec's Modifies anchors executable: existing catalog/entity members, git token purpose/fencing without provider requests, credential-board cells/profiles, git-only socket protocol, optional broker fakes, untouched non-vault probe fields, native invalid-model failures, existing board cells/settings content, in-transaction ruling rechecks, and unknown skip-reason interpolation. US-012 restores the spec-recommended en.json context file within the five-file cap. Complexity is reduced to medium for US-002/004 and complex for US-006/008 because they extend concrete existing patterns rather than introduce a new architecture; all credential/access-control/token/session stories retain the mandatory three-session-tdd security strategy. The apps/cli exclusion does not exclude the explicitly required koda-runner provider-cred/vault commands.

REPOSITORY AND DISCOVERY
This is an enhancement to an established Bun/Turborepo monorepo, not greenfield. Execution root: /Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/koda/repos/koda. codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this session; discovery used targeted Read/Grep/Glob instead. The supplied Express/Next.js detection is incorrect: .nax/mono/apps/api/context.md:19 identifies NestJS/Fastify/Prisma 7, and .nax/mono/apps/web/context.md:21 identifies Nuxt 4 SSR with root-level pages/components/composables. Runner is Bun-only ESM. Read the matching .nax/mono/apps/<app>/context.md before implementation; generated AGENTS.md files are not authoring sources. The API context requires nathapp-nestjs-patterns before NestJS coding; no matching skill file was exposed by repository discovery, so implementation must obtain it from its available skill host. The feature spec is .nax/features/provider-credential-vault/spec.md:1; approved design reference is docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-provider-credential-vault-design.md. All 15 story IDs, workdirs and dependencies are binding. Cross-package protocol and generated contract outputs remain in the specified API story workdirs; do not silently change dependencies or split stories.

ARCHITECTURE AND STORAGE
API owns persistence, permissions, scope resolution, attribution, and workflow decisions. Runner only transports requests and grants, caches them in memory, exposes per-job sockets, and connects the nax helper/session contracts. Web remains a Nuxt API client. No proxy, per-key budget system, or new secret backend. Reuse AES-256-GCM encryptToken/decryptToken at apps/api/src/common/utils/encryption.util.ts:7 and :32; encryptToken uses a random IV at :12 and emits iv:tag:ciphertext at :25. Add a separate providerCredentials namespace following apps/api/src/config/vcs.config.ts:5 and :32, with optional 64-hex env validation following apps/api/src/config/env.validation.ts:32. Register the new namespace in apps/api/src/app.module.ts:73; merely creating a config file will not load it. Missing master key must not prevent module construction or API boot. LocalSecretStore supplies randomized encryption plus deterministic 12-hex HMAC-SHA256 fingerprint and last4; do not substitute an unkeyed hash or reuse VCS_ENCRYPTION_KEY.
Add Prisma models and a committed additive migration in apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma, including inverse relations on Project (:125), FleetRepo (:794), and any chosen issue/job relation on FleetJob (:1052). Scope is a string constant/type, not a Prisma enum. The unique scopeKey/providerId pair avoids NULL uniqueness holes: global, project:<projectId>, repo:<repoId>. Project/repo foreign keys cascade as specified; actor IDs are plain strings. The issue unique tuple is jobId/credentialId/fingerprint, not epoch: retries and lease renewals must not duplicate attribution; rotating a key produces a new fingerprint attribution. Avoid coupling deletion to an issue FK policy that would prevent the required credential DELETE; durable FleetActivity is the usage record. Prisma generated imports must come from src/generated/prisma/client, with createPgAdapter for actual clients. Driver-adapter unique errors require isUniqueViolation rather than error.meta.target; see apps/api/src/vcs/prisma-vcs.repository.ts:4 and API context. Repositories use transaction-aware PrismaService as in apps/api/src/vcs/prisma-vcs.repository.ts:28-36. Export the service for consumers, not PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REPOSITORY; module DI tests must stay database-free and co-located. US-001 owns initial infrastructure, US-002 adds/exports the service.

MANAGEMENT, AUTHORIZATION, AND SECRET HYGIENE
Existing permission inventory already includes fleet.credential.read at apps/api/src/permissions/catalog.ts:199, and fleet.credential. is already high risk at :150. Add only the three new global writes to NEW_KEY_SCOPES (:116). Project credential read/create/update/delete are new project keys; add project.credential. to HIGH_RISK_PREFIXES (:142), preserving the low-risk read exception in the catalog's classification logic. Update catalog.spec.ts mirrored pins/counts and permissions/__snapshots__/role-matrix.json: global writes Owner/Admin only; Project Admin writes, other project roles read only. Guards remain authoritative on the API, with UI gating as affordance only. Cross-project and wrong-scope IDs must return 404, and repo membership must be checked when accepting repoId.
Approval writes must follow apps/api/src/vcs/vcs-route.commands.ts:44-69 for create and :73-103 for optional-key update: redactSecret replaces values before the approval body/hash/preview is stored; redemption seals the resubmitted secret, not the original one. Preserve an absent key in PATCH rather than manufacturing a redaction marker. Wire commands into ApprovalCommandRegistry and use @ApprovalGated({ redeem: true }), @ApprovalRedeemHeader(), ApprovalRouteGate; global gate projectId is null. Approval authorization must be re-evaluated through existing route-command principal machinery; do not insert a direct unguarded CRUD path. Management DTOs must be projections, never spread encrypted domain records: exactly id, scope, projectId, repoId, providerId, name, last4, fingerprint, disabled, createdBy, updatedAt. Validate providerId regex, name 1-64, key 16-8192 without whitespace at the shared domain boundary as well as DTO/form edges. Vault-off refuses ALL management writes with 503.
FleetActivityService.record at apps/api/src/fleet/activity/fleet-activity.service.ts:21 expects the mutating transaction and rejects key-like payload field names using /token|secret|key|password|credential/i at :15. Use only providerId, scope, name, fingerprint, never credentialId as a payload key or plaintext/ciphertext in audit summaries. Add provider_credential to the FleetEntityType union in US-003 and update the FleetActivity.entityType schema comment (apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:927); US-006 also uses that shared entity type and must remain buildable when run directly after US-002, without inventing a dependency on US-003. Register the additive union wherever first required without changing any existing member or delivering management routes early. Follow the atomic activity/audit precedent apps/api/src/fleet/repos/fleet-repos.service.ts:58-75. Preserve activity on credential deletion. API i18n is independent of web i18n: new providerCredentials files must actually resolve fleet.providerCredentials.* prefixes through the existing translation conventions, and both locales must be supplied.

SYNC, PROTOCOL, AND CONCURRENCY
packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts:235-247 contains TokenRequest/SyncRequest, :302-313 contains SyncResponse, and :82 contains threadModes capability. Add optional providerRequests/providerKeys/providerKeyErrors and providerVault, preserving every existing field and old-runner compatibility; no gratuitous protocol-version bump. API imports this workspace package type-only via its common/protocol bridge. US-006 owns provider wire types; US-007 may add the independent providerVault type field itself because it depends only on US-002, not US-006. apps/api/src/fleet/sync/sync-request.parser.ts:4 bounds token requests at 64, :57 parses token requests, and :70 parses the envelope: mirror this for provider requests with the strict providerId grammar and maximum 64.
SyncService at apps/api/src/fleet/sync/sync.service.ts:64 captures one sync time, :109 grants git tokens, :111 computes idle, and :129-172 fences token requests inside a transaction. Add provider handling with the same job row lock, FenceService and RUNNER_HELD_STATES checks before any key disclosure. A stale lease queues ABANDON and yields no grant; provider errors/grants both suppress long-polling. Keep provider issue insert and credential.issued activity in the same short transaction, skip duplicates safely (not a caught P2002 that leaves PostgreSQL transaction aborted), and never hold a transaction across notifier.wait or forge HTTP. A per-request failure should not expose secret-bearing error details or block unrelated job processing. Account is koda:<lowercase scope>:<name>; lease is exactly sync-time plus 600000 ms and wire expiry is ISO. Ciphertext failures yield none and a warning containing credential id only.
Thread credential scope MUST come from FleetThreadTurn -> ChatThread, not the synthetic ASSIGN repository. apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/prisma-fleet-job.repository.ts:265-272 currently provides findThreadTokenScope(kind/action); leave it unchanged and add findThreadCredentialScope(projectId/repoId) plus its domain interface. WORKSPACE anchor projectId is real and contributes the PROJECT override; PROJECT/WORKSPACE repoId is null. Update apps/api/src/fleet/sync/sync.module.ts:19 to import the provider service module, and update constructor fakes in sync-token-fence.spec.ts and sync.service.token-purpose.spec.ts without altering existing fence/token-purpose assertions.

BOARD AND VISIBILITY
apps/api/src/fleet/dashboard/credential-board.ts:54 currently derives provider rows only from runner profiles/credentials, :64 maps runner flags, and apps/api/src/fleet/dashboard/credential-board.service.ts:18 reads all runners. Add an explicit active-global-key input, providerVault boolean defaulting false, and kodaKeys projection; provider rows should include keys held only in koda so the UI can display them even when no runner advertises that provider. Vault off gives an empty kodaKeys list; no project/repo keys or plaintext may appear. DashboardModule at apps/api/src/fleet/dashboard/dashboard.module.ts:15 needs the service module dependency. Update CredentialBoardDto, fleet-openapi.contract.spec.ts property pins, credential-board.spec.ts shape expectations and service fakes, preserving existing cells/misfit logic and no placement preference.

RUNNER CREDENTIAL LIFECYCLE
apps/runner/src/credentials/broker.ts:26-36 defines CredentialProvider; new methods MUST be optional to preserve existing fakes. BrokerDeps at :50 gains an optional provider cache. Current servers map at :81 is git-only and release at :170-180 uses it to decide whether shared bin shims are still needed: a provider socket must live in a separate map. Serve irrespective of clone URL; current acquire parses HTTP clone URLs at :87 and therefore cannot be reused for SSH-only provider setup. Reuse socketPathFor/ensureSocketDir for deterministic job+epoch paths with the provider-keys discriminator. CredentialServer.listen at apps/runner/src/credentials/cred-server.ts:53 stages a private 0600 socket then atomically renames it; close at :86 inode-checks before unlinking to avoid deleting a restarted daemon's socket. Preserve that behavior in the sibling provider listener, and keep get-only git listener unchanged.
TokenCache at apps/runner/src/credentials/token-cache.ts:43, :50, :98 and :115 is the model for in-memory state, wake listeners, bounded requests, and matching responses to requested epochs. ProviderKeyGrant omits leaseEpoch: ProviderKeyCache must bind replies to the exact originating request snapshot, not the newest live job epoch; otherwise overlapping attempts can receive another attempt's secret. Cache scope is job/epoch/provider, with 60 s renewal margin and 55 s pending reply limit. Once a provider has been served, none must become revoked rather than decline, preventing accidental fallback to a different billing identity. An initial vault_off should allow helper decline as the spec failure table requires; a previously served source must still fail, not silently fall back. No key in journal, environment, filesystem, log, commands, or bundles. Only the socket path enters the nax environment.
